reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review contract, resource assessment rubric, fresh-review framework, Organization context and full StructureDefinition report, R4/R6 Organization and R6 ExtendedContactDetail definitions, and the direct OperationDefinition/SearchParameter findings whose `affectedResources` include Organization. Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were considered only as background because the reviewed resource is Organization.

r4Maturity.effectMd: Organization was trial-use/FMM 3 in R4, so compatibility for common administrative and directory data has meaningful stability pressure. This does not forbid remodeling, but it raises the burden for deleting common wire paths such as top-level `telecom` and `address` without a transition mechanism.

overall.oneLineConclusion: Organization keeps its resource identity but needs targeted migration for the R6 contact/address/telecom remodel; low-cost preservation of common R4 contact paths still matters.

reasoning.thesisMd: Organization is not removed or replaced, and many core fields remain stable, but R6 materially remodels the way official contact details are represented. Top-level `Organization.telecom` and `Organization.address` disappear, `Organization.contact` becomes `ExtendedContactDetail`, `contact.name` changes JSON shape, and R6 applies no-home constraints to the new contact container. For real directory, billing, reporting, and provider-routing datasets, that is enough to require a planned resource migration rather than a simple validator or codegen update.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The migration shape is a moderate targeted remodel, not a whole-resource redesign. Instances using only identifiers, name, type, active, aliases, partOf, or endpoint may require little structural work. Instances with the common address/telecom/contact surface need deliberate mapping: wrap former top-level contact points and addresses in contact entries, decide grouping rules, convert singleton contact names to arrays, and rebuild address-search indexes against the R6 path.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because typical Organization implementations will already need contact-model migration, preventing every local break has less leverage than it would on a mostly unchanged resource. That does not mean additional break prevention has no value. The deleted top-level `address` and `telecom` paths are common FMM 3 administrative data, so deprecated aliases, explicit transitional guidance, or dual-index search behavior could still materially reduce upgrade cost if the duplicate-representation tradeoffs are acceptable.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The strongest less-breaking candidates are transitional retention of `Organization.telecom` and `Organization.address`, or at least explicit compatibility guidance for aliases/search indexing. Those alternatives are not free: they create duplicate official-contact locations and require conflict, update, and search rules. By contrast, preserving the old local `Organization.contact` backbone would undercut the cross-resource `ExtendedContactDetail` goal, and weakening the no-home invariant would reduce the official-contact semantic cleanup. The `Measure/$collect-data` `practitioner` parameter rename has a much cheaper less-breaking path: keep `practitioner` as a deprecated alias for the Practitioner reporter case.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The direct behavior findings do not change the structural conclusion but do matter. The stable `Organization-address` search code now indexes `Organization.contact.address`, so search/index migration is coupled to the address move and can silently change result sets if data migration lags. The `Measure/$collect-data` provider filter change affects Organization as a possible reporter/provider and is an avoidable API compatibility issue. Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior issues are real base-platform concerns but are not Organization-specific resource-level drivers here.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The deterministic aggregate concluded `Partial`, `moderate-targeted-remodel`, and `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`. I agree with that result, but based on the substance rather than counts: the common top-level address/telecom removals and the contact datatype replacement drive targeted migration, while the same facts keep address/telecom compatibility preservation worth standards review.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for the StructureDefinition and behavior deltas because the package evidence is explicit. Uncertainty remains about the official work-group rationale, real-world prevalence of nested contact `home` use, and jurisdiction-specific use of organization qualifications.

findingConsiderations.title: Top-level Organization.telecom was removed and folded into Organization.contact.telecom
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a common old-valid/new-invalid wire break for official organization phone, email, fax, and URL data. It is one of the main reasons typical Organization instances need migration. Because a deprecated top-level alias is plausible, though not free, this remains standards-review-worthy rather than merely a local transform chore.

findingConsiderations.title: Top-level Organization.address was removed and folded into Organization.contact.address
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Organization addresses are common directory, billing, reporting, and routing data. Moving them under `Organization.contact.address` invalidates R4 instances and changes generated APIs and search indexing. The contact-based model is coherent, but a transitional retained/deprecated `address` path or explicit dual-index guidance is worth revisiting because of the field's prevalence.

findingConsiderations.title: Organization.contact changed from a local backbone component to ExtendedContactDetail, changing codegen and contact.name JSON shape
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The reusable datatype replacement is the center of the remodel and creates generated-code and JSON-shape migration, especially `contact.name` object-to-array conversion. I treat this as probably proportionate once the R6 shared-contact model is accepted, but it still makes a resource-level migration program necessary for contact-using implementations.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 newly forbids home-use telecom and address values inside Organization.contact
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a real old-valid/new-invalid validator break for a narrower pattern. It should be handled explicitly in migration scans, but it does not materially alter the resource-level conclusion and appears proportionate to the official-organization-contact semantics.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds Organization.qualification, creating substantial R6-to-R4 structured data loss risk
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This optional addition does not make R4 instances invalid in R6, so it does not drive the R4-to-R6 migration-program judgment. It still matters for safety/business governance because qualification, accreditation, status, period, and issuer data can be regulatory or directory-trust content that needs explicit R6-to-R4 mapping.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds Organization.description, which has no core R4 Organization counterpart
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is an optional additive R6 field with only ordinary downgrade/round-trip loss risk. It does not invalidate R4 data and should not materially influence the resource-level break-avoidance posture beyond documenting downgrade policy when description text matters.

findingConsiderations.title: The `practitioner` filter is removed in favor of broader reporter/provider parameters
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This direct behavior finding includes Organization because R6 adds broader reporter/provider support. It does not drive Organization structure migration, but it is a low-cost avoidable API break: keeping `practitioner` as a deprecated alias for Practitioner reporters would avoid client failure or silent query broadening while preserving the broader R6 reporter model.

findingConsiderations.title: Many stable search codes now index different R6 element paths after resource model changes
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: For Organization, the stable address search code moves from `Organization.address` to `Organization.contact.address`. This is mostly a consequence of the structural remodel, but it is operationally important because clients may keep using the same query code while servers silently index a different path.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a generic Resource-level operation issue, not an Organization-specific change. It should be reviewed and mitigated at the shared API/platform layer, and I did not count it as a driver of the Organization resource migration conclusion.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Revisit whether R6 should preserve `Organization.telecom` and `Organization.address` as deprecated transitional aliases, or publish explicit rationale and compatibility guidance explaining why duplicate official-contact locations are too costly.

Publish and test a concrete Organization migration map: move top-level telecom/address into `contact`, define grouping and conflict rules, convert `contact.name` to an array, rebuild Organization address search indexes, and require an explicit policy for nested `home` contact uses.

For `Measure/$collect-data`, preserve `practitioner` as a deprecated alias for `reporter=Practitioner/...` or require strict warning/error behavior so stale R4 clients do not silently collect broader provider data.

Define downgrade/round-trip mappings for `Organization.qualification` and, where needed, `Organization.description`, preferably with standard extensions or IG guidance so credentialing and directory-disambiguation data is not silently flattened or lost.

caveats: This review is based on the local R4/R6 package definitions and reports; it did not include separate official work-group rationale beyond the supplied evidence.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were treated as context only and should be resolved in their own base behavior reviews.

Real-world prevalence for nested `home` organization contacts and R6 organization qualification exchange is uncertain, so those items are migration-policy priorities rather than primary resource-level drivers.
